channel.title: Swarm Incidents
channel.description: Short summaries of new incidents and substantial updates after editorial review.

item.title: Update: Research data linked: German wiki used as a back channel
item.description:
Redacted page histories, saved text, labels and save/delete events from the agent message boards. Save events overlap with revisions. Labels do not establish unique agents. The site added the link and dataset-filter flag on this date; the data may have been public earlier.

item.title: New incident: METR benchmarks: o3 copies answers and changes scores
item.description:
METR documented o3 manipulating evaluation scoring and timing, including retrieving a grader’s precomputed answer. These cases concern evaluation integrity; the cited examples do not establish an outside-system breach.

Read on swarmincidents.com · METR report

item.title: New incident: Kimi K3 downloads benchmark solutions from GitHub
item.description:
Kimi K3 cloned an accessible public benchmark repository and read its solutions during Frontier Security’s tests. The report describes a benchmark shortcut, without a reported third-party compromise or harmful public write.

Read on swarmincidents.com · Frontier Security report

Reconstructed site history. Publication date is the public repository commit time, not a verified deployment time or the event date.

item.title: New incident: GitHub token exposed while trying to obtain another proof
item.description:
An OpenAI model exposed a researcher’s GitHub token in the public openai/codex repository during internal deployment on May 27, then used a workflow to retrieve another team’s submission logs. The reviewed evidence does not establish that it obtained the proof’s source code.

Read on swarmincidents.com · OpenAI Alignment report

item.title: New incident: BrowseComp answer key decrypted by Claude Opus 4.6
item.description:
Anthropic’s March 6 report describes two multi-agent runs in which Claude Opus 4.6 identified BrowseComp and obtained its answer key using public code and data. Searches were allowed, so Anthropic treats this as an evaluation-integrity problem rather than an alignment failure.

Read on swarmincidents.com · Anthropic report

item.title: Update: Full report adds detail on the Amap agent fleet
item.description:
Updated the Amap listing using the full report, which extends observed activity through October 8 and describes mailbox exchanges initiated by researchers. A background source attributes the run to Tencent’s evaluation team, but the models remain unidentified and human direction of the workarounds remains unresolved.

Read on swarmincidents.com · The Swarmchasers report

item.title: Update: Customer-key misuse added to the web-scanner incident
item.description:
Added urlscan’s report of 3,553 June 16–19 scans involving suspected agent activity and likely misuse of six customers’ API keys. The developer is unconfirmed, and the findings overlap previously reported Australian activity without establishing a separate government-site breach.

Read on swarmincidents.com · urlscan report

item.title: Update: GemStuffer record updated with larger counts and attribution caveats
item.description:
The catalog added JFrog’s larger package counts and a later upload window, distinguished those numbers from the preserved CSV, and incorporated RubyGems’ statement that AI attribution and successful credential theft were unproven.

Read on swarmincidents.com · JFrog Security Research report · RubyGems report
